topic.title: VACNET и античит Dota 2: что обновилось на самом деле

evidence.heading: Confirmed Dota 2 anti-cheat and enforcement facts
evidence.excerpt: No primary Valve source in the verified set says that the CS2-branded VAC Live/VACNET pipeline is deployed in Dota 2.

evidence.heading: Cheaters Will Never Be Welcome in Dota, 21 February 2023
evidence.excerpt: Valve permanently banned more than 40,000 accounts and described a honeypot: client data normal play never read but the exploit did.

evidence.heading: Gameplay Update, 28 February 2023
evidence.excerpt: Valve disabled the record command, many console commands that exposed client state, and pregame access to player profiles in matchmaking. This corrects the March 2024 date in the initial brief.

evidence.heading: Smurfing is Not Welcome in Dota, 1 September 2023
evidence.excerpt: Valve permanently banned 90,000 smurf accounts, traced them to main accounts, and described possible penalties from behavior-score adjustments to permanent bans.

evidence.heading: Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC)
evidence.excerpt: Steam Support provides the broad VAC definition; this does not establish the CS2 VAC Live/VACNET pipeline in Dota 2.

evidence.heading: VAC and server-check concept links
evidence.excerpt: The graph supports only a high-level client/server/behavioral model and explicitly forbids operational evasion guidance.

evidence.heading: Historical CS:GO VacNet compute figures
evidence.excerpt: The approximately 600,000 matches, four CPU-minutes per match, and 1,700 CPU figures are from 2018 CS:GO reporting, not Dota 2 and not 2026.

evidence.heading: Product mapping
evidence.excerpt: Dota 2 articles use Melonity; claims must remain high-level, sourced, and free of safety guarantees or evasion details.

strict_rules: State plainly that VAC Live/VACNET is not publicly confirmed for Dota 2.
Do not attribute the 40,000 bans or 90,000 smurf detections to VACNET or a neural network.
Present server-signal categories only as expert hypotheses, not Valve's published checklist.
Do not provide operational anti-cheat evasion or cheat-implementation instructions.
